resources.string: Setup
Execution
Instructions for this exercise are not available in this version. Follow your own setup and technique, and use a load you can control.
Close
Lie on the bench with your eyes beneath the bar. Plant both feet, settle your upper back on the pad, and take an even grip just wider than shoulder width. Unrack the bar with your arms extended.

Lower the bar under control toward the middle of your chest, keeping your wrists over your elbows. Touch lightly without bouncing, then press up until your arms are extended. Keep your shoulders settled against the bench.

Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, then lie back and hold them beside your chest. Plant both feet and keep your upper back supported. Turn your palms forward or slightly inward, whichever feels comfortable.

Press both dumbbells upward over your chest without letting them collide. Lower them under control until your elbows are beside or slightly below your torso, within a comfortable range. Keep both sides moving smoothly.

Place your hands on the floor a little wider than shoulder width and extend your legs behind you. Brace your trunk so your head, hips and legs form a steady line. Use an elevated hand support if needed to make the movement manageable.

Bend your elbows and lower your chest between your hands while keeping your body in one line. Stop at a comfortable depth, then press the floor away to return to the start. Avoid letting your hips sag or rise ahead of your shoulders.
Stand with the bar at your upper chest and take a balanced grip just outside your shoulders. Set your feet comfortably, keep your trunk steady, and position your elbows slightly in front of the bar.

Press the bar overhead in a controlled path, moving your head clear as the bar passes. Finish with the bar balanced over your shoulders and feet, without forcing your lower back to arch. Lower it smoothly to your upper chest.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and support yourself with the other hand on a stable bench or surface. Set your feet securely and keep your back steady, with the working arm hanging below your shoulder.

Draw the dumbbell toward your hip, keeping your elbow close to your side. Pause briefly without twisting your torso, then lower the weight until your arm is extended. Complete the repetitions on one side before switching.

Sit facing the cable station and secure your thighs beneath the pads. Take the bar with an even, comfortable overhand grip. Sit tall and let your arms extend overhead without losing a steady torso position.

Pull the bar down toward your upper chest while keeping your torso mostly upright and your elbows moving down. Return the bar overhead slowly until your arms extend comfortably. Do not swing or pull the bar behind your neck.
Sit facing the cable station with feet on the supports and knees slightly bent. Take the handle with both hands and sit tall, allowing your arms to reach forward while keeping your torso steady.

Draw the handle toward your lower ribs, moving your elbows back without leaning to create momentum. Briefly settle your shoulder blades, then let the cable carry your hands forward under control while maintaining your seated position.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand beside your thighs. Keep a soft bend in your elbows and choose a load you can lift without swinging. Set your feet comfortably and keep your torso steady.

Raise your arms out to the sides in a smooth arc, leading with your elbows. Stop around shoulder height or sooner if that is your comfortable range. Lower the dumbbells slowly; avoid shrugging or using momentum.

Set the bar securely across your upper back and take an even grip. Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, or in a stance that lets you squat comfortably. Brace your trunk and make sure the bar is stable before stepping back.

Bend your hips and knees together, keeping your whole foot in contact with the floor. Descend only as far as you can maintain a steady position, then stand by pushing through the floor. Keep the bar balanced over your mid-foot.

Hold one dumbbell vertically close to your chest with both hands supporting it. Stand with your feet in a comfortable squat stance and brace your trunk. Keep the weight close rather than letting your arms drift forward.

Bend your hips and knees to lower between your legs while keeping the weight close to your chest. Use a depth where your balance and torso remain controlled, then stand smoothly. Keep your feet grounded throughout.
Stand with a barbell held in front of your thighs and feet about hip width apart. Keep your knees softly bent, arms long and trunk braced. Begin with the bar close to your body.

Push your hips back and let the bar slide close down your thighs and shins. Keep your back steady and knees softly bent; stop when your hamstrings limit the hinge or your position would change. Drive your hips forward to stand tall without leaning back.

Adjust the machine so its pivot is near your knee and the roller rests comfortably against the backs of your lower legs. Set the seat and supports, then hold the handles with your hips supported against the pad.

Bend your knees to draw the roller through a comfortable range without lifting your hips. Pause briefly, then extend your legs slowly until they return to the starting position. Keep the movement smooth rather than letting the stack drop.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms by your sides and palms facing forward or slightly inward. Keep your feet steady, shoulders relaxed and elbows near your torso.

Bend your elbows to curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders without rocking your torso. Keep your upper arms mostly still, then lower the weights under control until your arms are extended comfortably.
Stand facing the cable with the attachment set around chest height. Hold it with both hands, elbows bent and close to your sides. Set your feet securely and keep your torso steady.

Straighten your elbows to press the attachment down while keeping your upper arms near your sides. Finish in a comfortable extension, then bend your elbows slowly to return. Avoid leaning your body onto the handle.
Stand on a level floor with a dumbbell in each hand beside your thighs. Set your feet about hip width apart and keep your knees softly extended. Choose a load that lets you balance without rocking.

Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels while keeping your torso steady. Pause briefly, then lower your heels to the floor under control. Keep the dumbbells beside your body and avoid bouncing.

Adjust the standing calf raise machine so the shoulder pads rest comfortably on your shoulders. Select or rack the load according to the machine, then stand with the balls of your feet on its platform and hold the handles. Lift into a steady position and release the safety catch if present.

Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet, keeping your knees softly extended and your torso steady. Pause briefly, then lower your heels through a comfortable range without bouncing. Re-engage the safety catch if present before stepping off.
Hold a pull-up bar with a secure, comfortable grip and let your body hang without swinging. Keep your shoulders controlled and legs together, with knees straight or softly bent as needed.

Lift your legs by bringing your thighs toward your torso without building momentum. Raise only through a range you can control, then lower slowly until your body is still. Bend your knees if that helps maintain control.

Practise the setup with a load you can control before increasing it. Keep the bar close, establish a steady trunk position before lifting, and reset between repetitions rather than rushing the next pull.
Practise the hip hinge before adding heavier load. Keep the bar close and stop the descent before you lose control of your trunk position; reaching the floor is not the goal.
Practise the hip hinge with light dumbbells first. Keep them close to your legs and limit the descent to the range you can control; do not reach lower by changing your trunk position.
Technique considerations
Set an adjustable bench to a low incline and sit with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs. Lie back and bring the dumbbells beside your upper chest, feet planted and upper back supported.
Press both dumbbells up over your upper chest, keeping your wrists steady. Lower them under control until your elbows are beside your torso, then press again without clashing the weights.
Place your hands on a bench, step or low platform a little wider than shoulder width and extend your legs behind you. Brace your trunk so your head, hips and legs stay in one line.
Lower your chest toward the raised support by bending your elbows, keeping your body straight. Press back up until your arms are extended. A higher support makes the movement easier.
Set both cable pulleys around chest height and take a handle in each hand. Stand a step forward with one foot slightly ahead, elbows softly bent, and let your arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles toward each other in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping your elbows softly bent. Squeeze briefly, then let your arms open under control until you feel a comfortable stretch.
Anchor a resistance band behind you at chest height and hold one end in each hand beside your chest. Stand with a stable stance and keep your shoulders settled.
Press your hands forward until your arms are extended, keeping the band under tension. Return slowly until your hands are beside your chest without letting the band snap back.

Grip parallel bars and lift yourself to a supported position with your arms extended. Keep your shoulders settled down away from your ears and your legs under control. Use an assisted dip machine or band if bodyweight is too much.

Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are around horizontal or a comfortable depth. Press back up until your arms are extended. Keep the descent controlled rather than dropping into it.
Stand with your feet about hip width apart holding a barbell with an overhand grip. Hinge at your hips until your torso is inclined, keep a steady trunk, and let the bar hang below your shoulders.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows back, keeping your torso angle steady. Lower the bar under control until your arms are extended. Avoid jerking the bar with your lower back.
Reach up and grip a pull-up bar with your hands a little wider than shoulder width, palms facing away. Hang with your arms extended and shoulders controlled, legs together or softly bent.

Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down until your chin approaches the bar, or as high as you can control. Lower slowly to a full hang without swinging. Use assistance if you cannot control the descent.
Grip a pull-up bar with your palms facing you and your hands about shoulder width apart. Hang with your arms extended and your shoulders settled, keeping your body still.
Pull yourself upward until your chin nears the bar, keeping your elbows moving down and back. Lower under control to a full hang. Add assistance if the movement is not yet controllable.
Anchor a resistance band at waist or chest height and hold one end in each hand. Step back until the band is under light tension, soften your knees and keep your trunk steady.
Pull your hands toward your ribs by driving your elbows back, keeping your shoulders down. Return slowly until your arms are extended and the band is still taut.
Hold a light resistance band in front of you with both hands about shoulder width apart and your arms extended. Stand tall with your ribs down and your shoulders relaxed.

Open your arms by pulling the band apart until it nears your chest, keeping your elbows softly bent. Return slowly to the start without letting the band snap. Use a lighter band rather than shrugging.
Sit or stand with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward or slightly inward. Keep your trunk steady and your upper back supported if seated.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are extended, without clashing them overhead. Lower under control until your elbows are around shoulder height or a comfortable depth.

Set a cable pulley low and hold the handle with the hand furthest from the machine, or use a light single-hand setting. Stand side-on with the cable crossing in front of your body and a soft elbow bend.
Raise your arm out to the side until it is around shoulder height, leading with your elbow. Lower under control to the start. Keep the movement smooth rather than swinging the weight up.
Set a cable pulley around face height and attach a rope. Hold one end in each hand with your thumbs pointing back, arms extended, and stand with a stable stance.

Pull the rope toward your face by driving your elbows out and back, finishing with your hands beside your head. Return under control until your arms are extended. Use a load that lets you keep your shoulders relaxed.
Stand upright holding a barbell with an underhand grip about shoulder width apart. Keep your elbows near your sides and your trunk steady.
Bend your elbows to curl the bar toward your chest without swinging your torso. Lower the bar under control until your arms are extended. Keep your wrists in line with your forearms.
Stand on the middle of a resistance band or anchor it low, and hold one end in each hand with your palms facing up. Keep your elbows beside your torso and stand tall.
Curl your hands toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still. Lower slowly against the band's tension until your arms are extended.
Hold a single dumbbell with both hands, or one dumbbell in each hand, and raise it overhead with your arms extended. Keep your elbows pointing forward and your trunk steady.
Bend your elbows to lower the weight behind your head through a comfortable range. Straighten your elbows to return overhead. Keep your upper arms from drifting outward.
Lie on the bench and grip the bar with your hands about shoulder width apart. Settle your upper back, plant your feet, and unrack with your arms extended.
Lower the bar toward your lower chest with your elbows close to your torso. Touch lightly, then press up until your arms are extended. Keep your wrists steady over your forearms.

Rest the bar across the front of your shoulders with your elbows high and your hands outside your shoulders, or use a crossed-arm grip. Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and brace your trunk.
Squat down by bending your knees and hips while keeping your torso upright and your elbows lifted. Descend to a comfortable depth, then drive up through your feet to standing.
Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and your toes pointing slightly out. Keep your arms in front of you or at your sides for balance and brace your trunk.
Bend your knees and hips to sit down and back while keeping your heels down. Descend to a comfortable depth, then stand up and finish tall. Use a chair or support if you need help with balance.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Stand about a stride in front of a bench and place one foot on it behind you with your toes down. Set your front foot flat and keep your torso steady.

Bend your front knee and hip to lower your body, keeping your front heel down and your torso upright. Descend to a comfortable depth, then drive up through your front foot. Use a lower support if balance is difficult.

Sit in the leg press machine with your back and hips against the pad and your feet flat on the platform about shoulder width apart. Select a load you can control and release the safeties according to the machine.

Press the platform away by straightening your knees, stopping before your knees lock hard. Lower under control until your knees are around a right angle or a comfortable depth, keeping your back on the pad.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs and your feet about hip width apart. Soften your knees slightly and brace your trunk before hinging.
Push your hips back and lower the dumbbells along your legs, keeping them close and your back steady. Stop where your hamstrings feel loaded, then stand up by driving your hips forward.
Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet and grip it just outside your legs. Bend your knees, set your trunk steady and take the slack out of the bar before lifting.
Push the floor away and stand up with the bar close to your legs, keeping your trunk position steady. Lower the bar by hinging your hips and bending your knees once it passes them, then reset.
Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a padded bar across your hips. Plant your feet about hip width apart so your shins are close to vertical at the top.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is roughly level with your thighs. Squeeze briefly, then lower under control without letting the bar roll.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor about hip width apart. Keep your arms beside you and your ribs settled.
Press through your heels to lift your hips until your thighs and torso form a steady line. Pause briefly, then lower under control. Avoid arching your lower back to gain height.
Stand with your feet a little wider than hip width and the kettlebell on the floor in front of you. Hinge at your hips, take the handle with both hands and set your trunk steady.
Hike the bell back between your legs, then drive your hips forward to swing it up to around chest height. Let it return as you hinge again, keeping your arms relaxed and your back steady.
Stand on a level floor with your feet about hip width apart and your knees softly extended. Use a wall or rail for balance if you need it.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as you can control. Pause briefly, then lower your heels to the floor slowly. Avoid bouncing.
Set your forearms on the floor with your elbows under your shoulders and extend your legs behind you onto your toes. Brace your trunk so your head, hips and heels form a line.
Hold the position while breathing steadily and keeping your hips from sagging or rising. End the hold when you can no longer keep the line rather than pushing into your lower back.
Kneel facing a high cable pulley and hold the rope beside your head. Set your hips in place and keep your elbows forward.
Curl your torso down by drawing your ribs toward your hips, keeping your hips still. Return under control until your trunk is upright, without pulling with your arms.
Stand or sit with a dumbbell in each hand and your palms facing your body. Keep your elbows near your sides and your trunk steady.
Bend your elbows to raise the dumbbells toward your shoulders, keeping your palms facing in. Lower under control until your arms are extended without swinging your torso.
Stand or sit holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing up. Keep your elbows beside your torso and your shoulders relaxed.
Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still. Lower slowly until your arms are extended.
Sit at the end of a bench holding a bar with an underhand grip about shoulder width apart. Brace your upper arms against your thighs or a supported pad so your elbows stay in place.
Curl the bar up by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms supported. Lower under control until your arms are extended, stopping before your elbows are forced straight.
Sit at a lat pulldown station and take a close grip on the bar or handle. Secure your thighs under the pad and keep your torso upright.
Pull the handle toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down, keeping your torso steady. Return under control until your arms are extended overhead.
Sit at a lat pulldown station and take a wide overhand grip on the bar. Secure your thighs under the pad and keep your torso upright.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and slightly back. Return under control until your arms are extended, without leaning back to move the load.
Set the bench to a low incline and lie back with your eyes beneath the bar. Plant your feet, settle your upper back and take an even grip just wider than shoulder width.
Lower the bar under control toward your upper chest, keeping your wrists over your elbows. Touch lightly, then press up until your arms are extended.
Set the bench to a decline and secure your legs as the bench provides. Lie back, settle your upper back and take an even grip just wider than shoulder width.
Lower the bar under control toward your lower chest, keeping your wrists steady. Touch lightly, then press up until your arms are extended. Use a spotter or safeties when working near your limit.
Stand holding an EZ bar with an overhand grip a little narrower than shoulder width. Let the bar hang in front of your thighs and keep your trunk steady.
Raise the bar along your body by leading with your elbows, stopping around chest height or wherever you can keep your shoulders comfortable. Lower under control to the start.
Sit on a bench holding an EZ bar with an underhand grip on the angled sections. Let your upper arms rest beside your torso and keep your back steady.
Curl the bar toward your chest by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still. Lower under control until your arms are extended.
Stand inside a trap bar with your feet about hip width apart and take the handles at your sides. Bend your knees, set your trunk steady and take the slack out of the bar.
Push the floor away and stand up with the bar close to your body, keeping your trunk position steady. Lower under control by hinging your hips and bending your knees, then reset.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and your feet about hip width apart. Brace your trunk and keep your gaze forward.
Step forward and lower your body by bending both knees until your front thigh is around parallel or a comfortable depth. Push through your front foot to return, then repeat on the other side.
Stand with the bar resting across the front of your shoulders and your hands just outside shoulder width. Brace your trunk, keep your feet about hip width apart and your elbows slightly forward.
Press the bar overhead until your arms are extended, moving your head slightly back so the bar clears your face. Lower under control to your shoulders and keep your trunk steady throughout.
Kneel on a mat and grip the ab roller handles under your shoulders. Brace your trunk and begin with the roller close to your knees.
Roll the wheel forward only as far as you can keep your trunk steady and your hips from sagging. Pull it back under control to the start. Keep the range short rather than reaching for distance.
Sit in the leg extension machine with your back against the pad and the roller on your lower shins. Align your knees with the machine's pivot and select a load you can control.
Straighten your knees to lift the roller, stopping before your knees lock hard. Lower under control until your knees are bent comfortably. Avoid swinging the weight up.
Stand with your feet about hip width apart holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side. Keep your other hand on your hip or at your side and brace your trunk.
Bend sideways toward the weighted side through a comfortable range, keeping your hips steady. Return slowly to upright. Use a light load rather than pulling yourself further with momentum.
Stand or sit with one dumbbell held overhead in both hands, or one in each hand, and your arms extended. Keep your elbows pointing forward and your trunk steady.
Bend your elbows to lower the weight behind your head through a range you can control. Straighten your elbows to return overhead without letting your upper arms drift outward.
Stand with a light dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs. Keep your elbows softly bent and your trunk steady.
Raise the dumbbells forward to about shoulder height, lower them, then raise them out to the sides to the same height. Use a light load so each phase stays controlled.

Set the chains so they rest on the floor at the bottom of the press and load the bar accordingly. Lie on the bench with your feet planted, upper back settled and an even grip just wider than shoulder width.
Lower the bar under control toward the middle of your chest as the chains take load. Touch lightly, then press up until your arms are extended, keeping your shoulders settled.
Set both cable pulleys around chest height and take a handle in each hand. Stand a step forward with one foot slightly ahead and your elbows bent beside your chest.
Press both handles forward until your arms are extended, keeping your trunk steady. Return under control until your hands are beside your chest without letting the cables pull you back.
Set up facing a wall with your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width and your heels against the wall. Build up to an inverted position you can hold steadily before adding repetitions.

Bend your elbows to lower your head toward the floor through a range you can control. Press back up to full extension. Use a box or pike position instead if you cannot hold the inverted position steadily.
Place your hands on a low bench or step about shoulder width apart and extend your legs behind you. Brace your trunk so your body stays in one line.
Lower your chest toward the bench by bending your elbows, then press back up until your arms are extended. Keep your hips in line with your shoulders throughout.
Place your hands on a low bench or step noticeably wider than shoulder width and extend your legs behind you. Brace your trunk so your body stays in one line.
Lower your chest toward the bench by bending your elbows, then press back up until your arms are extended. Keep the wider hand position comfortable rather than forcing extra range.
Start in a push-up position with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a line. Brace your trunk and keep your feet about hip width apart for stability.
Perform one push-up, then shift your weight onto one hand and rotate into a side plank with the other arm reaching up. Return to the push-up position and alternate sides.
Place your hands on the floor wider than shoulder width and extend your legs behind you. Brace your trunk so your head, hips and legs form a line.
Lower your chest between your hands by bending your elbows, then press back up until your arms are extended. Keep the wider grip comfortable rather than forcing extra depth.
Start in a push-up position with one hand under your shoulder and the other arm out to the side or behind your back. Set your feet wider apart than usual to help your balance.
Lower your chest under control by bending the supporting elbow, then press back up. Keep the movement small at first and use an elevated support if the position is not steady.
Set a cable pulley low and hold a handle in each hand at shoulder height, or use a single handle per arm. Stand with a stable stance and your trunk braced.
Press the handles upward until your arms are extended, keeping the cables under tension. Lower under control until your hands are back at shoulder height.
Set the dip machine's assist or load according to its design, then take the handles with your arms extended. Keep your shoulders settled and your trunk steady.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms are around horizontal or a comfortable depth. Press back up until your arms are extended, without dropping into the bottom.
Hold a kettlebell in each hand at your shoulders with your elbows slightly forward. Stand with your feet about hip width apart and your trunk braced.
Dip slightly at your knees, then drive upward and press both kettlebells overhead until your arms are extended. Lower them under control to your shoulders.
Stand with the bar across the front of your shoulders and your hands just outside shoulder width. Brace your trunk and keep your feet about hip width apart.
Dip a short distance at your knees, drive upward and press the bar overhead as your legs extend. Lower the bar under control to your shoulders and reset before the next repetition.
Stand with the bar resting behind your neck across your upper shoulders and your hands a little wider than shoulder width. Brace your trunk and use a load you can control comfortably.

Dip slightly at your knees, drive upward and press the bar overhead through a comfortable range. Lower it under control behind your neck, and shorten the range or use a lighter load if the position feels strained.
Sit facing away from a low cable pulley with a handle in each hand at shoulder height. Keep your back supported and your trunk steady.
Press the handles overhead until your arms are extended, keeping the cables under tension. Lower under control until your hands return to shoulder height.
Stand on the middle of a resistance band, or anchor it under your feet, and hold one end in each hand at shoulder height. Keep your trunk steady and your feet about hip width apart.
Press your hands overhead until your arms are extended, keeping the band under tension. Lower under control until your hands return to shoulder height without letting the band snap down.
Stand with the bar across the front of your shoulders, hands just outside shoulder width, and your feet about hip width apart. Brace your trunk and keep your legs still.
Press the bar overhead until your arms are extended, moving your head slightly back so the bar clears your face. Lower under control to your shoulders without using your legs to drive the bar.
Hinge at your hips with a barbell held in a wide overhand grip until your torso is inclined. Let the bar hang below your chest and keep your trunk steady.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest by driving your elbows out to the sides. Lower under control until your arms are extended, keeping the wide grip and steady torso.
Stand with a barbell in an overhand grip and hinge at your hips until your torso is inclined. Keep your trunk steady and let the bar hang below your shoulders.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows back, keeping your torso angle from rising. Lower it under control until your arms are extended.
Set a bench to a low incline and lie chest-down with a dumbbell in each hand hanging below you. Plant your feet and keep your chest supported.
Pull both dumbbells toward your ribs by driving your elbows back. Lower them under control until your arms are extended, keeping your chest on the bench.
Place one hand and the same-side knee on a bench with the other foot on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in the free hand below your shoulder and keep your back steady.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip by driving your elbow back, keeping your torso still. Lower under control until your arm is extended, then repeat or change sides.
Stand side-on to a low cable pulley and take the handle in the hand furthest from it. Step back into a staggered stance with the cable across your body and your trunk steady.
Pull the handle toward your hip by driving your elbow back. Return under control until your arm is extended, keeping your torso from rotating with the cable.
Straddle the T-bar or landmine bar with the handle in both hands and your feet about hip width apart. Hinge at your hips with your trunk steady and your knees softly bent.
Pull the handle toward your chest by driving your elbows back, keeping your torso angle steady. Lower under control until your arms are extended.
Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip about shoulder width apart. Let it hang in front of your thighs and keep your trunk steady.
Raise the bar along your body by leading with your elbows to around chest height, or wherever your shoulders stay comfortable. Lower under control to the start.
Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley and stand facing it with an overhand grip. Keep your trunk steady and your feet about hip width apart.
Raise the bar along your body by leading with your elbows to around chest height, or wherever your shoulders stay comfortable. Lower under control while keeping the cable taut.
Sit at a lat pulldown station and take a close overhand grip on the bar. Secure your thighs under the pad and keep your torso upright.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down. Return under control until your arms are extended overhead.
Sit at a lat pulldown station and take an overhand grip on the bar. Secure your thighs under the pad and let your arms extend fully overhead at the start.
Pull the bar to your upper chest through the full range, then return until your arms are fully extended overhead. Keep your torso upright rather than leaning back.
Sit or kneel at a lat pulldown station with a single handle. Take the handle in one hand with your arm extended overhead and your torso steady.
Pull the handle toward your shoulder by driving your elbow down and back. Return under control until your arm is extended, then repeat or change sides.
Sit at a lat pulldown station and take an underhand grip about shoulder width apart. Secure your thighs under the pad and keep your torso upright.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down. Return under control until your arms are extended overhead.
Attach a V-bar to a lat pulldown station and sit with your thighs secured. Take the handles with your arms extended overhead and your torso upright.
Pull the handles toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down. Return under control until your arms are extended.
Take the parallel V-bar handles at a pull-up station with your arms extended. Hang with your shoulders controlled and your legs together or softly bent.
Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down until your chest nears the handles, or as high as you can control. Lower slowly to a full hang without swinging.
Sit at a lat pulldown station and take a wide overhand grip with your thighs secured. Keep your torso upright and your neck relaxed forward.

Pull the bar down behind your head only through a comfortable range, or keep it in front of your neck if that feels easier. Return under control until your arms are extended, without forcing the bar lower.
Grip a pull-up bar with a wide overhand grip and hang with your arms extended. Keep your shoulders controlled and your torso steady.
Pull yourself up toward the bar through a comfortable range, keeping your neck relaxed. Lower under control to a full hang, and use a narrower grip if the wide position feels strained.
Set a sturdy box at a height that lets you reach a comfortable sitting position. Stand with the bar across your upper back, your feet about shoulder width apart and your trunk braced.
Sit back and down until you settle lightly on the box, keeping your heels down. Drive up through your feet to standing without rocking off the box first.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and your feet about shoulder width apart. Brace your trunk and keep your chest up.
Bend your knees and hips to sit down and back, keeping your heels down and the dumbbells beside you. Descend to a comfortable depth, then stand up and finish tall.
Set your back against the machine's pad with your shoulders under the shoulder pads and your feet flat on the platform about shoulder width apart. Release the safeties according to the machine.
Bend your knees and hips to lower your body along the pad to a comfortable depth. Drive through your feet to stand, keeping your back on the pad throughout.
Kneel on a mat with the bar across your upper back and your hands holding it in place. Keep your trunk upright and your hips above your knees.
Sit your hips back toward your heels through a range you can control, keeping your trunk steady. Drive your hips forward to return to the kneeling start.
Set the bar across your upper back, high enough that your torso can stay upright, with your hands just outside your shoulders. Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and brace your trunk.
Squat down with an upright torso and your heels down, descending only as far as you can keep your trunk position. Drive up through your feet to standing.
Hold the bar overhead with your arms extended and your hands wide enough to keep the bar steady. Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and brace your trunk.
Squat down while keeping the bar balanced over your mid-foot and your trunk upright. Descend only as far as you can hold the position, then stand up.
Stand with the bar across the front of your shoulders and your hands just outside shoulder width. Brace your trunk with your feet about hip width apart.

Dip at your knees, drive upward and press the bar overhead as you drop into a squat to receive it. Stand up with the bar overhead, or use a shallow dip and press if the receiving position is not comfortable.
Set the band under your feet and across the bar so it adds tension as you stand. Place the bar across your upper back, brace your trunk and set your feet about shoulder width apart.
Squat down under control to a comfortable depth, keeping your heels down. Drive up through your feet against the increasing band tension to standing.
Stand on a resistance band with your feet about hip width apart and bring it across the back of your shoulders. Hold it in place and brace your trunk.
Hinge at your hips to lower your torso while keeping your back steady and your knees softly bent. Return to standing by driving your hips forward against the band.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and a padded bar across your hips. Plant your feet about hip width apart and hold the bar steady with your hands.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso and thighs form a steady line. Pause briefly, then lower under control without letting the bar roll.
Stand facing a low cable pulley and take the handle with both hands. Set your feet about hip width apart and hinge at your hips with your trunk steady.
Stand up by driving through your feet and bringing your hips forward, keeping the handle close to your legs. Lower under control by hinging your hips again.
Set the band under your feet and around the bar so it adds tension at the bottom. Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet and grip it just outside your legs.
Push the floor away and stand up with the bar close to your legs, keeping your trunk steady against the band tension. Lower under control and reset between repetitions.
Set the chains so they rest on the floor at the bottom of the lift and load the bar accordingly. Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet and grip it just outside your legs.
Push the floor away and stand up as the chains take load, keeping the bar close to your legs. Lower under control and reset before the next repetition.
Stand on a stable platform or plate low enough that you can still set your trunk position comfortably. Place the bar over the middle of your feet and grip it just outside your legs.
Push the floor away and stand up with the bar close to your legs, keeping your trunk steady through the extra range. Lower under control and reset.
Set the bar across your upper back with your hands holding it in place. Stand with your feet about hip width apart and soften your knees slightly.
Hinge at your hips to lower your torso while keeping your back steady, descending only as far as you can control. Drive your hips forward to return to standing.

Stand with your feet noticeably wider than shoulder width and your toes turned out, with the bar over the middle of your feet. Take a grip inside your legs, set your trunk steady and take the slack out of the bar.
Push the floor away and stand up with the bar close to your body, keeping your knees tracking over your toes. Lower under control and reset between repetitions.
Set the bar across your upper back with your hands holding it in place. Stand tall with your feet about hip width apart and brace your trunk.
Step forward and lower your body by bending both knees to a comfortable depth. Push through your front foot to return, then repeat on the other side.
Set the bar across your upper back and stand facing a sturdy box or bench at a height where your knee is around hip level when your foot is on it. Place one foot on the box and brace your trunk.
Drive through the foot on the box to step up and stand tall. Step down under control and repeat, using a lower box or bodyweight if the step is not steady.
Set the bar across your upper back with your hands holding it in place. Stand tall with your feet about hip width apart and brace your trunk.
Step forward into a lunge to a comfortable depth, then push up and step through into the next lunge on the other side. Keep each step controlled rather than rushing the stride.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and your feet about hip width apart. Brace your trunk and keep your gaze forward.
Step back and lower your body by bending both knees to a comfortable depth. Push through your front foot to return, then repeat or change sides.
Stand facing a sturdy box or bench with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Place one foot on the box and brace your trunk.
Drive through the foot on the box to step up and stand tall. Step down under control and repeat, using a lower box if the step is not steady.
Set the bar across your upper back and place the top of one foot on a low bench behind you. Set your front foot flat and keep your torso steady.
Bend your front knee and hip to lower your body, keeping your front heel down. Descend to a comfortable depth, then drive up through your front foot.
Hold a kettlebell in one hand at your side and stand tall with your feet about hip width apart. Brace your trunk and keep your gaze forward.
Step forward into a lunge, then pass the kettlebell under your front leg to the other hand as you step through. Keep each step and hand-off controlled rather than rushing the switch.
Stand facing a sturdy box or bench at a height where your knee is around hip level when your foot is on it. Place one foot on the box and brace your trunk.
Drive through the foot on the box to step up, then lift the other knee toward your chest while standing tall. Lower the leg and step down under control before repeating.
Sit on a bench with the balls of your feet on a stable raised platform and a padded bar across your lower thighs. Hold the bar steady with your hands and keep your knees bent.
Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet, letting your heels drop below the platform at the start. Pause briefly at the top, then lower under control.
Sit in the calf press machine with the balls of your feet on the platform and your knees softly extended. Select a load you can control and release the safeties according to the machine.
Press the platform away with your ankles to extend your feet, keeping your knees still. Return under control until your heels are comfortably stretched, without bouncing.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a stable step or low platform and hold a dumbbell in one hand for balance or support. Keep your knees softly extended.
Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet, then lower them under control through a comfortable range. Keep your balance steady rather than bouncing.
Stand on the middle of a resistance band with the balls of your feet and hold the ends, or loop it over your forefoot. Keep your knees softly extended and your balance steady.
Raise your heels against the band's tension, pause briefly, then lower under control. Keep the movement smooth rather than bouncing at the bottom.
Sit in the seated calf raise machine with the balls of your feet on the platform and the pad across your lower thighs. Release the safeties according to the machine and keep your knees bent.
Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet, then lower under control until your heels are comfortably stretched. Avoid bouncing out of the bottom.
Set the Smith machine bar at a height where it rests across your upper back when you stand with the balls of your feet on a stable platform. Keep your knees softly extended and your trunk steady.
Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet, then lower them under control through a comfortable range. Keep the bar steady on your back throughout.
Set the bar across your upper back as for a squat and stand with the balls of your feet on a stable step or platform. Keep your knees softly extended and your balance steady.
Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet, pause briefly, then lower under control. Keep your trunk steady rather than bouncing the weight.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and your feet about hip width apart on a level floor or a stable step. Keep your knees softly extended.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels, pause briefly, then lower under control. Keep the dumbbells beside your body and avoid bouncing.
Set both cable pulleys high and take a handle in each hand. Stand a step forward with one foot slightly ahead, elbows softly bent and your arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles down and together in front of your hips or chest, keeping your elbows softly bent. Return under control until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest.
Set both cable pulleys high and take a handle in each hand with your arms open wide. Stand a step forward with your trunk steady and your elbows softly bent.
Bring the handles together and slightly across your body in a wide arc, then return under control. Keep the range comfortable rather than forcing your arms further back.
Lie back on a decline bench with a dumbbell in each hand above your chest and your palms facing each other. Plant your feet and keep your elbows softly bent.
Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest. Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest without clashing them.
Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand above your chest and your palms facing each other. Plant your feet and keep your elbows softly bent.
Open your arms out to the sides through a comfortable range, then bring the dumbbells back together above your chest. Keep your elbows softly bent throughout.
Set both cable pulleys low and take a handle in each hand, or set them high and step forward. Keep your elbows softly bent and your trunk steady.
Bring the handles together in front of your upper chest in a wide arc, then return under control. Keep the range comfortable rather than reaching further behind you.
Lie back on a low incline with a dumbbell in each hand above your upper chest and your palms facing each other. Plant your feet and keep your elbows softly bent.
Open your arms out to the sides until you feel a comfortable stretch, then bring the dumbbells back together above your upper chest. Keep the elbows softly bent.
Lie back on a low incline with a dumbbell in each hand above your upper chest, palms facing you. Plant your feet and keep your elbows softly bent.
Open your arms out to the sides, turning your palms forward as you descend. Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest and return the palms to face you.
Set both cable pulleys low and take a handle in each hand. Stand a step forward with one foot slightly ahead, elbows softly bent and your arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles up and together in front of your upper chest in a wide arc. Return under control until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest.
Stand or sit at a preacher bench with the cable's straight bar in an underhand grip. Rest your upper arms on the pad so your elbows stay in place.
Curl the bar up by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms on the pad. Lower under control until your arms are extended, stopping before your elbows are forced straight.
Sit on a bench with your knees apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand. Rest the back of that upper arm against your inner thigh so the elbow stays in place.
Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm against your thigh. Lower under control until your arm is extended, then repeat or change sides.
Stand holding an EZ bar by the angled sections with an underhand grip. Keep your elbows near your sides and your trunk steady.
Bend your elbows to curl the bar toward your chest without swinging your torso. Lower under control until your arms are extended.
Lie back on a low incline with a dumbbell in each hand hanging beside your body and your palms facing in. Keep your upper arms still and your shoulders supported.
Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders while keeping your palms facing in. Lower under control until your arms are extended without letting your elbows drift forward.
Lie on your back with your head near a low cable pulley and take the bar or handle with an underhand grip. Rest your upper arms beside your torso.
Curl the handle toward your chest by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still. Lower under control while keeping the cable taut.
Stand facing away from a high cable pulley with a handle in each hand and your elbows raised beside your head. Keep your upper arms steady and your trunk braced.
Curl the handles toward your head by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms in place. Return under control until your arms are extended.
Stand facing a low cable pulley and take the bar with an overhand grip. Keep your elbows near your sides and your trunk steady.
Curl the bar upward by bending your elbows, keeping your wrists in line with your forearms. Lower under control while keeping the cable taut.
Lie chest-down on an incline bench and hold an EZ bar by the angled sections with your arms hanging below you. Keep your upper arms still against the bench.
Curl the bar toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms in place. Lower under control until your arms are extended.
Anchor a resistance band above and behind you, or stand on it, and hold the ends with your elbows bent beside your head. Lie back or stand with your upper arms steady.
Straighten your elbows to press the band forward and up, keeping your upper arms in place. Return under control until your elbows are bent comfortably.
Lie on your back with your head near a low cable pulley and take the handle with both hands. Hold it above your chest with your elbows bent and pointing up.
Straighten your elbows to extend the handle upward, keeping your upper arms still. Return under control until your elbows are bent comfortably.
Stand side-on to a cable pulley with a single handle in one hand and your elbow bent beside your head or your side. Keep your upper arm steady and your trunk braced.
Straighten your elbow to extend the handle, keeping your upper arm in place. Return under control until your elbow is bent comfortably, then repeat or change sides.
Lie on a bench holding an EZ bar by the angled sections above your chest with your arms extended. Keep your elbows pointing up and your feet planted.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead or just behind your head, through a range you can control. Straighten your elbows to return, keeping your upper arms still.
Stand facing a low cable pulley and take the handle with both hands behind your head, elbows bent. Keep your upper arms beside your head and your trunk steady.
Straighten your elbows to press the handle forward and up, keeping your upper arms in place. Return under control until your elbows are bent comfortably.
Lie on a bench holding an EZ bar above your chest with your arms extended. Keep your elbows pointing up and your feet planted.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead through a range you can control, then straighten them to return. Keep your upper arms still rather than flaring your elbows outward.
Sit on a bench and hold one dumbbell with both hands above your head, arms extended. Keep your elbows pointing forward and your back supported.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head through a comfortable range. Straighten your elbows to return overhead, keeping your upper arms steady.
Hinge forward slightly with a dumbbell in one hand and your upper arm close to your torso, elbow bent. Brace your other hand on a bench if that helps you stay steady.
Straighten your elbow to move the dumbbell back behind you, keeping your upper arm still. Return under control until your elbow is bent comfortably, then change sides.
Stand facing a cable pulley at chest height with a single handle in the hand opposite it, or use both arms with two pulleys. Keep your elbow softly bent and your trunk steady.
Open your arm out to the side and slightly back through a comfortable range, keeping your elbow softly bent. Return under control without letting your torso rotate.
Stand facing away from a low cable pulley with the handle in one hand in front of your thigh. Keep your elbow softly bent and your trunk steady.
Raise your arm forward to about shoulder height, keeping your elbow softly bent. Lower under control to the start without swinging your torso.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs and your elbows softly bent. Keep your trunk steady and your shoulders relaxed.
Raise one or both dumbbells forward to about shoulder height, then lower under control. Keep the movement smooth rather than swinging the weights up.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing your body. Keep your elbows softly bent and your trunk steady.
Raise both dumbbells forward together to about shoulder height. Lower them under control to your thighs without leaning back.
Lie chest-down on an incline bench with a light dumbbell in each hand hanging below you. Keep your elbows softly bent and your chest supported.
Raise your arms out to the sides through a comfortable range, leading with your elbows. Lower under control until your arms hang again.
Stand with a dumbbell in one hand at your side and your other hand free for balance. Keep your elbow softly bent and your trunk steady.
Raise your arm out to the side to about shoulder height, leading with your elbow. Lower under control to the start, then repeat or change sides.
Hinge forward at your hips with a dumbbell in each hand hanging below your shoulders and your elbows softly bent. Keep your trunk steady.
Raise your arms out to the sides through a comfortable range, leading with your elbows. Lower under control until your arms hang again.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and your elbows softly bent. Keep your trunk steady and your shoulders relaxed.
Raise both arms out to the sides to about shoulder height, leading with your elbows. Lower under control without swinging the weights up.
Anchor a resistance band low to one side and loop it around the ankle nearest it, holding a support for balance. Stand tall with your weight on the other leg.
Draw the banded leg across the front of your body against the band's tension, keeping your trunk upright. Return under control, then repeat or change sides.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor about hip width apart. Keep your arms beside you and your ribs settled.
Press through your heels to lift your hips until your thighs and torso form a steady line. Pause briefly, then lower under control without arching your lower back.
Stand side-on to a low cable pulley with the cuff around the ankle furthest from it, holding the frame for balance. Keep your trunk upright and your weight on the other leg.
Draw the banded leg across the front of your body against the cable's tension, keeping your trunk still. Return under control, then repeat or change sides.
Lie on your back with your legs extended and your hands beside your hips or under your lower back. Brace your trunk so your lower back stays settled.
Lift your legs together to a height you can control without your lower back arching, then lower slowly. Reduce the range or bend your knees if your back lifts.
Lie face-down in the leg curl machine with the roller on your lower calves and your knees just past the pad edge. Hold the handles and keep your hips down.
Bend your knees to curl the roller toward your hips through a comfortable range. Lower under control until your legs are extended, keeping your hips on the pad.
Sit in the seated leg curl machine with the pad on your lower calves and your thighs secured. Align your knees with the machine's pivot and release the safeties.
Bend your knees to draw the pad under you through a comfortable range. Return under control until your legs are extended, without letting the weight snap back.
Lie on your back with one knee bent and that foot flat on the floor, and the other leg extended or raised. Keep your trunk steady and your arms beside you.
Press through the supporting heel to lift your hips until your body forms a steady line. Pause briefly, then lower under control and change sides.
Stand at the leg curl machine with the pad behind one ankle and your thighs against the support. Hold the frame for balance and keep your trunk upright.
Bend your knee to curl the pad toward your hips through a comfortable range. Return under control until your leg is extended, then repeat or change sides.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor. Rest your hands beside your head or across your chest and settle your lower back.
Curl your shoulders off the floor by drawing your ribs toward your hips, keeping your chin relaxed. Lower under control without pulling on your head.
Lie back on a decline bench with your legs secured and your hands beside your head or across your chest. Settle your lower back against the pad.
Curl your shoulders up by drawing your ribs toward your hips, keeping your chin relaxed. Lower under control without pulling on your neck.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and your hands beside you. Bring your knees toward your chest so your hips start slightly lifted.
Curl your hips off the floor by drawing your knees toward your chest, using your trunk rather than momentum. Lower under control until your hips return to the floor.
Kneel facing a high cable pulley and hold the rope beside your head. Set your hips in place and keep your elbows forward.
Curl your torso down by drawing your ribs toward your hips, keeping your hips still. Return under control until your trunk is upright.
Lie on your back with your hands beside your hips and your legs extended. Brace your trunk so your lower back stays settled.
Raise your legs slightly and alternate crossing one over the other through a small range. Keep your lower back from arching and stop before you lose control.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor. Rest your hands across your chest or beside your head and settle your lower back.
Curl and then rise until your torso is upright, keeping your chin relaxed. Lower under control without pulling on your head or swinging your arms.
Stand or kneel with your trunk upright and your shoulders relaxed. Breathe out steadily and let your ribs settle.
After breathing out, draw your abdomen in gently and hold briefly without letting your ribs flare. Release and breathe normally before repeating.
Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms reaching overhead. Brace your trunk so your lower back stays settled.
Curl your shoulders up and reach your hands toward your toes through a comfortable range. Lower under control without straining your neck.
Lie on a flat bench with a cable handle in each hand and your arms above your chest, elbows softly bent. Plant your feet and keep your shoulders supported.
Open your arms out to the sides through a comfortable range, then bring the handles together above your chest. Keep your elbows softly bent throughout.
Stand side-on to a cable pulley at chest height with a single handle in the hand furthest from it. Keep your elbow softly bent and your trunk steady.
Bring the handle across your body in a wide arc in front of your chest, then return under control. Keep your torso from rotating with the cable.
Sit facing a low cable pulley and take the handle in one hand with your arm extended. Keep your trunk upright and your legs braced.
Pull the handle toward your ribs by driving your elbow back, keeping your torso still. Return under control until your arm is extended, then repeat or change sides.
Lie on the floor with a dumbbell in each hand beside your chest and your elbows resting on the floor. Plant your feet and keep your upper arms at roughly 45 degrees to your torso.
Press both dumbbells upward until your arms are extended, then lower under control until your upper arms rest on the floor. Let the floor set the bottom of the range.
Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your shoulders, palms facing you. Keep your back supported and your trunk steady.
Press the dumbbells upward while turning your palms forward. Lower under control, turning your palms back toward you, until your hands return in front of your shoulders.
Place one hand and the same-side knee on a bench with the other foot on the floor. Hold a kettlebell in the free hand below your shoulder and keep your back steady.
Pull the kettlebell toward your hip by driving your elbow back, keeping your torso still. Lower under control until your arm is extended, then repeat or change sides.
Stand on one leg holding a kettlebell in the opposite hand, with a soft knee and your trunk braced. Let the kettlebell hang in front of your standing leg.

Hinge at your hip to lower the kettlebell along your standing leg while your free leg extends behind you. Stand up under control, then repeat or change sides. Use a light load and a fingertip support if balance is uncertain.
Lie back on a low incline with a dumbbell in each hand hanging beside you and your palms facing forward. Keep your upper arms still and your shoulders supported.
Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders by bending your elbows. Lower under control until your arms are extended without letting your elbows drift forward.
Stand facing a low cable pulley with the cuff around one ankle, holding the frame for balance. Keep your trunk steady and your weight on the supporting leg.
Move the banded leg back by extending your hip through a comfortable range, keeping your trunk still. Return under control, then repeat or change sides.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and your hands beside your head. Bring your shoulder blades off the floor and keep your lower back settled.
Draw one knee toward your chest while turning the opposite shoulder toward it, then alternate. Keep the movement controlled and avoid pulling on your neck.
Sit in the pec deck machine with your back against the pad and your forearms or hands on the pads. Align the seat so the handles are around chest height and release the safeties.
Bring the pads together in front of your chest, keeping your elbows softly bent. Return under control until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest.
Sit facing the reverse fly machine with your chest against the pad and your hands on the handles. Keep your elbows softly bent and your trunk steady.
Open your arms out to the sides through a comfortable range, leading with your elbows. Return under control until your hands come back together.
Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up and wrists just past your knees. Keep your forearms still.
Curl your wrists upward through a comfortable range, keeping your forearms on your thighs. Lower under control until your wrists return to the start.
Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing down and wrists just past your knees. Keep your forearms still.
Extend your wrists upward through a comfortable range, keeping your forearms on your thighs. Lower under control until your wrists return to the start.
Stand with a dumbbell in each hand beside your thighs and your feet about hip width apart. Let your arms hang straight and keep your trunk steady.
Raise your shoulders toward your ears through a comfortable range, without bending your elbows. Pause briefly, then lower under control.
Stand holding an EZ bar in front of your thighs with your arms extended. Keep your feet about hip width apart and your trunk steady.
Raise your shoulders toward your ears through a comfortable range, keeping your arms straight. Pause briefly, then lower under control.
Stand inside a trap bar with the handles at your sides and your arms extended. Keep your feet about hip width apart and your trunk steady.
Raise your shoulders toward your ears through a comfortable range, keeping your arms straight. Pause briefly, then lower under control.
Stand holding a barbell in front of your thighs with your arms extended. Keep your feet about hip width apart and your trunk steady.
Raise your shoulders toward your ears through a comfortable range, keeping your arms straight. Pause briefly, then lower under control.
Kneel or sit on a padded surface and rest your forehead on a folded towel or pad. Support your weight with your hands and keep your neck in a comfortable position.
Apply gentle pressure through your forehead, holding briefly without forcing. Release and rest between repetitions. Keep the effort small and skip the movement if the position feels uncomfortable.
Sit or stand upright with one hand resting against the side of your head. Keep your shoulders relaxed and your trunk steady.
Tilt your head gently toward your hand while your hand resists, holding briefly without forcing. Return to upright and repeat or change sides. Use light pressure only.
